decisions.summary: Rendered guard messages are kept in each tree's own git dir (hooks-test/messages/), found by one resolver (l7r-guard messages store, git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) that both the hooks-test and guard-messages recipes use.
decisions.why: This is the task line's own fix (reproduce with two worktrees, then key the store by tree), and it corrects a defect: a check reading another tree's renderings tells a builder nothing is owed when wordings are owed, or turns red on a guard the tree does not hold.

decisions.summary: dev/guard-messages.tsv, the reviewed record, stays one tracked file.

decisions.summary: The tree's store is made to match this run's roster: a file of no suite on the run's list is removed, so a rendering from a guard the tree no longer holds is not judged.
decisions.why: This fixes the second fault the plan found (messages::corpus read every .jsonl in the directory, not the run's roster), which is a check passing or refusing on the wrong input. It is red first in test-parts.3.sh.

decisions.summary: Suite freshness stamps stay shared across worktrees (stamps per tree was priced and not taken). A green job also writes <common dir>/hooks-test/rendered/<job>@<key>.jsonl, and a suite is skipped only where a rendering at its stamp's key exists. A gather step fills a skipped suite's files from that keyed rendering.
decisions.why: This keeps the existing measured saving (commit d7456c4c8d, 5 of 46 suites rerun, 83 s against 151 s) and stops it from defeating the per-tree store. Declining per-tree stamps leaves existing behavior that works as it is. It carves nothing out of the fix, because each tree is still judged on its own content's renderings.

decisions.summary: If a skipped suite's keyed rendering was replaced by another tree's run between the skip and the gather, the run fails by name and names the fix (make hooks-test again, which reruns that suite).
decisions.why: This is a loud, self-healing failure in a narrow race, not a wrong outcome. The run never judges stale or foreign renderings, so the defect the task fixes is not carried forward. Rerunning the suite automatically instead is a design choice, not a fidelity question.

decisions.summary: Each clone's first make hooks-test after landing reruns every suite once (about 160 s, measured 2026-11-26), plus one extra launcher call per run.
decisions.why: This is a one-off cost of the fix, not a narrowing. The plan measured and labeled it.

decisions.summary: scripts/land-alone.sh and scripts/gates/review-tree.sh stop copying the common hooks-test/ into their tree's git dir.
decisions.why: Under the new layout that copy would fill the tree's store with the clone's renderings before the tree's own run, which is the same defect again, so removing it is part of the fix. Note: the search that showed nothing else read the copy (grep -rn hooks-test rust scripts tests) does not cover the Makefile. The plan covers the Makefile's recipe by a separate statement (it reads the stamps from the common directory since d7456c4c8d). Even if a missed reader existed, dropping the copy could only cost reruns, never a wrong verdict.

decisions.summary: Nothing is found and left. The task is classed as not performance work.
decisions.why: No known defect is deferred. The shared-stamp saving is kept rather than added to, so calling it a correctness fix is accurate.

decisions.summary: A quoted or backticked phrase that is the subject of 'does/did ask you' is blanked with its verb before spans are blanked; the session's own 'I do ask you' still fires.
decisions.why: T282: a report describing an ask's wording was read as an ask. Removing a statement the detector misread serves the GM's 2026-11-26 words ('I would prefer not to see these messages about false positives') and FR-002's narrow detector. The rule is bounded by the span, and the true-ask twin is pinned. Nothing FR-002 or amendment 1 owes the filter is exempted.

decisions.summary: The '?' rule skips a last sentence running from 'asks:'/'asks whether'/'asks if' to its '?' with no you/your and no other '?' on the line.
decisions.why: It removes the check-described-by-its-question false firing from the corpus. Four twins that put something to him still fire and are pinned, including a reported question addressed to 'you' and a second question on the line. Only statements leave the detector's reach.

decisions.summary: The '?' rule skips items of a 2+ item all-'?' list under a lead-in naming a checklist, or naming what something has/asks/holds/lists/poses/carries/answers, when the lead-in names neither the GM nor the session.
decisions.why: It removes the listed-checklist false firing. Lists put to him all still fire and are pinned: 'Two questions for you:', 'Open questions:', 'I have two questions...', a mixed list, a single item, no lead-in, and question-word items with suite case 9 kept. This is precision on statements and does not narrow FR-002's asks.

decisions.summary: 'waiting (on|for) you' is a measurement when a time count or share is the past-tense subject of was/were and the clause ends or goes on to another figure.
decisions.why: It removes the two time-breakdown figure firings. Work put to him ('Two hours of review are waiting on you', 'waiting on your budget answer', present tense, count of things) still fires and is pinned in the Rust test. It is bounded on both sides.

decisions.summary: 'with waiting on you kept/counted/... separate/apart/...' names a breakdown category.
decisions.why: It removes the 'Blocking minutes, with waiting on you kept separate:' firing. The twins 'Two tasks are waiting on you, kept separate below.' and 'with waiting on you: the budget's words.' still fire. It reaches statements only.

decisions.summary: STATED's 'needs your words' becomes 'words?' so 'What needs your word: ...' is caught; pinned in both suites.
decisions.why: This is a widening: a true ask HEAD's guard passed (a check passing bad work, a defect). Fixing it enforces FR-002 and narrows nothing. It was measured on both corpora: no T235 firing changes, and one already-firing message's quoted line moves.

decisions.summary: Both refusals gain 'If the line puts nothing to him (offers him nothing), go on and say nothing of this to him.'; reviewed by message-check.
decisions.why: This sentence directly carries 'I just don't want to see the explanation of the false positives reach me'. A line that puts nothing to him owed the filter nothing, so 'go on' restates FR-002's scope and is no carve-out from it. The GM's words take as given that sessions recognize false firings; what he struck is their explanation reaching him. Goal item 1 keeps every true ask refused until filtered. decisions.summary: The restated morning offer still fires; recognizing an ad-hoc escalation-check's kept verdict needs a new record and is filed as T335, landing before T302.

decisions.summary: The GM's question is answered with the measured rate, 33% before and 8% after on the 28 firings with no T lost, against 'under about one false firing in five'.

decisions.summary: The plan shows no ask is lost with two firings-only corpora (the 28 of 2026-11-25/26 and T235's labeled 112) through the fixed guard, plus pinned true-ask twins for every rule, and does not run a fresh recall sample.
decisions.why: FR-002 (429) asks for a detector measured for hit rate, a sample of hits, and recall on an independently labeled sample. decisions.summary: Synchronize the checks' compiling cargo calls through a counted set of machine-wide flock slots under ~/.cache/l7r-build-slots/, freed when the holder dies, no daemon; the builder count itself is not capped
decisions.why: This is the GM's request as written (2026-11-26): 'address that with some synchronization rather than pre-emptively limiting builders just in case'. A counted lock on the coinciding compiles is that synchronization, and builders past the count queue only for the compile.

decisions.summary: Every cargo call through cargo_in except cargo fmt, plus cover.rs's coverage build, takes a slot; fmt, llvm-cov show-env/report, cargo --version and direct test-binary runs do not
decisions.why: 'That' in the GM's words is the compiles coinciding. Leaving out the calls that do not compile drops nothing the request reaches, and the measurement puts the peaks in coinciding cover-builds.

decisions.summary: L7R_BUILD_SLOTS defaults to 2 (labeled GUESS) and caps compiling calls at once, not builders; 0 means no slot
decisions.why: A semaphore has to have a count. The default comes from the measured peak (three compiles at once, about 15 rustc each on 22 cores) rather than from a builder cap, and the 0 escape and the knob keep it a tunable piece of synchronization, not a pre-emptive limit on builders.

decisions.summary: If the slot directory cannot be made, a slot file cannot be opened or flock cannot start, the call runs without a slot and says so on stderr
decisions.why: Physically impossible case: when the lock primitive is missing there is nothing to synchronize on. The alternatives are refusing, which is a red gate for a throughput control (nothing in request.md asks for that), or hanging. The stderr notice keeps it visible.

decisions.summary: A wait past L7R_BUILD_SLOT_CEILING (900 s, GUESS) runs the call without a slot, written as a slot-wait line of code 1 with an audit reopen on one such line in a week
decisions.why: Purpose ground: the request is for synchronization that lets more builders work, and an endless wait would let one hung cargo stop every tree's checks for good, which defeats that purpose concretely. The plan states the cost, prices the alternatives and names a falsifier. Aside, non-blocking: 'a pass is then one more compile at once, three' holds for a single pass only. Several starved waiters passing at once under four or five builders are not bounded by it; the slot-wait code-1 lines and the audit's reopen are what would show that.

decisions.summary: Cargo started by a holder carries L7R_BUILD_SLOT_HELD, and a gate run under it takes no slot; a call holds one slot and never waits for a second; the run lock is taken first and the slot inside it
decisions.why: This is deadlock avoidance inside the mechanism. The nested run is already counted under its parent's slot, so no compile goes unsynchronized and the request's reach is not narrowed.

decisions.summary: The wrapper's own tool build (scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh build) takes no slot
decisions.why: The bootstrap argument does not hold, because the slot is a flock program call that shell can make. 'Shell, no Phase line' is implementation cost and is no ground either. The one ground that survives is the measurement: where no check's phase ran, the samples top out at 2.6 GiB and 13 rustc, against 5.9-6.4 GiB where coverage builds coincide (measured 2026-11-26). So leaving this build unslotted does not bring back the coincidence the request is about. The limits are real. The figure is joint with the guard build and comes from one three-builder run, and this is a compile whose coincidence still grows with the builder count. The ruling stands on that measurement and falls with it: the plan's own reopen condition (the re-measurement showing one at a peak) is the right trigger, and the candidate it names should be filed if that happens.

decisions.summary: The hook suites' guard build takes no slot
decisions.why: Ruled on its own, on the same and only surviving ground: the measured ceiling of the no-phase samples (2.6 GiB and 13 rustc, measured 2026-11-26) bounds this build too, well below the coinciding-cover-build peaks. Shell-only is cost, not a ground. This ruling also falls with that measurement, and the three- and four-builder re-measurement is what tests it.

decisions.summary: T284's line's re-measurement of three and four code builders with the slot is not done in this task; the coordinating session runs it once the slot has landed, and docs/process-decisions.md records it as owed
decisions.why: Physical ground: measuring several builders 'with it' needs the slot in every builder's tree, which only a landing gives, so the task cannot do it before it lands. FR-009's filed-task-id rule covers deferred defects, and this is not one. But the payoff of the GM's request (builders no longer pre-emptively limited) arrives only with this re-measurement. Landing T284 alone leaves the builder cap of two in place until it is run and recorded.

decisions.summary: A wait writes one Phase line, step slot-wait, read as its own category ('waiting on a build slot', first of PHASE_COLUMNS) in make task-time and make where-time, with a notice each minute naming the holders; a lint, test build or test run's phase spans its wait and the readers subtract it, while a coverage build's slot is taken before its clock starts
decisions.why: This serves the GM's standing 2026-11-22 words: 'we want everything measured so we know where our time goes, especially for compiling'. A new wait that went unbooked would go against that. Where the clock boundary falls is design, and the readers take the wait out.

decisions.summary: Tests run with Slots::off() and the slot's own tests use a scratch directory; a landing's gate takes the same slot as a builder's
decisions.why: The landing's gate is part of what the cap was protecting ('their compiles and a landing's gate would not coincide'), so covering it keeps the request whole. Tests keeping off ~/.cache is hygiene and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Recorded in dev/audits/build-slot.md (measurement, falsifier, cost, alternatives), docs/process-decisions.md and rust/gate/CLAUDE.md; no make target and no guard added
decisions.why: The audit entry with a falsifier answers the GM's 2026-11-25 register words ('what we would look at that would falsify the notion that this is a good idea'). Adding no target or guard adds nothing the request did not ask for.

blocks: ### T284 (2026-11-26: nothing kept two trees' compiles apart, so the builder count was capped by the chance that they coincide - three builders' anonymous memory peaked at 6.4 GiB of the container's 10 and load at 94 on 22 cores, measured 2026-11-26, `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once")

decisions.summary: Every compiling cargo call of the checks takes a slot (clippy, test builds, cargo test, test --doc, test-times' build, hamlet's cargo run, the coverage build); cargo fmt, llvm-cov show-env/report, cargo --version and direct test-binary runs take none
decisions.why: Which calls the synchronization covers is a mechanism choice inside the GM's 'some synchronization'; the calls left out do not compile, so nothing the request is about is excluded.

decisions.summary: A slot is the flock of a file slot-<i> under ~/.cache/l7r-build-slots/, signed with its holder, freed when the holder dies; no daemon
decisions.why: This is the synchronization the GM asked for in place of a builder cap.

decisions.summary: L7R_BUILD_SLOTS, default 2, labeled GUESS; it caps compiling cargo calls at once, not builders; 0 means no slot
decisions.why: It caps coinciding compiles, not builders. Extra builders edit, test and run coverage freely and queue only where their compile would coincide, which is the opposite of 'pre-emptively limiting builders'. The 0 switch only turns the mechanism off.

decisions.summary: Poll every 0.5 s (GUESS); a waiter says it waits each minute, naming the holders
decisions.why: These are mechanism parameters, and the waiter's notice makes a wait visible.

decisions.summary: A cargo started by a holder carries L7R_BUILD_SLOT_HELD and a gate run under it takes no slot
decisions.why: Holding a slot for a nested run is physically impossible without deadlock: the inner run would wait on the slot its own parent cargo test holds. Its compiles already sit inside the parent's slot, so nothing goes unsynchronized.

decisions.summary: A slot directory that cannot be made, a slot file that cannot be opened or a flock that cannot start lets the call run without a slot, said on stderr
decisions.why: Synchronization is physically impossible when the lock cannot be had at all. Refusing would turn a throughput control into a red gate, and waiting would hang every tree. A caveat: the block writes the code-1 slot-wait line for a wait that ended without a slot, so a call that fell open with no wait may show only on stderr. Writing that line here too would let the audit's one-a-week reopening see it.

decisions.summary: A waiter past L7R_BUILD_SLOT_CEILING (900 s, GUESS) runs without a slot, said on stderr and written as a slot-wait line of code 1; dev/audits/build-slot.md reopens the count on one such line in a week
decisions.why: In the hung-holder case the block names, holding the rule literally defeats the request's purpose: one hung cargo would stop every tree's checks for good, which is worse than the builder cap the slot replaces. Rejected alternatives were priced: wait without end, or refuse as the run lock does. The block's sentence 'a waiter passes it only when both slots stay held for 900 s on end, which is two holders each longer than the longest compile measured' overclaims, and the claim is unmeasured. Waiters are not served in arrival order. Each 0.5 s poller races the others, and a tree that releases a slot and starts its next compiling cargo call at once tries again immediately. So under sustained contention (four or more builders, cold trees) a turning-over queue can keep one waiter out for 900 s with no holder hung. This is not ruled a defect: such a pass yields one extra compile, three at once, the measured peak level, with no wrong outcome; it is recorded as code 1 and reopens the count. The sentence should be restated to say so. Counting the ceiling only while the slots' holder signatures stay unchanged would confine the pass to a hung holder; that is offered as an option, not required.

decisions.summary: The wrapper's own tool build (scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh build) takes no slot
decisions.why: 'Shell, writes no Phase line' is a cost argument and is not credited. The ground credited is measured: where no check's phase ran, the samples top out at 2.6 GiB and 13 rustc, against 5.9-6.4 GiB where three coverage builds coincided. So this build is not the coincidence the request addresses, and no wrong outcome has been shown. The falsifier is stated: the owed re-measurement showing one at a peak. A caveat: that 2.6 GiB is one joint figure for both unslotted builds, taken at three builders only, so the four-builder re-measurement is what confirms it.

decisions.summary: The hook suites' guard build takes no slot
decisions.why: Ruled separately from the wrapper build, on the same measured ground: the joint 2.6 GiB / 13 rustc ceiling where no check's phase ran, against 5.9-6.4 GiB at the coinciding coverage builds. No wrong outcome has been shown, and the re-measurement at three and four builders, owed by T284's own line, is the named falsifier. Unlike the wrapper build, nothing physically prevents a shell flock here, so this ruling rests on the measurement alone and should be revisited if the re-measurement shows one at a peak.

decisions.summary: The re-measurement at three and four builders, the rest of T284's line, is not done in this landing; the coordinating session runs it with the slot landed and records the count in docs/process-decisions.md
decisions.why: A re-measurement 'with it' physically cannot run until the slot is live in every tree, which means after this landing, and dispatching three or four builders is the coordinating session's work. Recording it as owed in process-decisions.md keeps it alive. An aside: the block says no other task carries it, and the builder cap stays at two until someone runs it, so filing it as its own line would keep it from being lost when T284 is ticked.

decisions.summary: A call that waited writes one Phase line (step slot-wait, code 1 where it ran without a slot); columns::category books it as 'waiting on a build slot' first of PHASE_COLUMNS; a lint's or test build's phase span includes its wait and the readers subtract it
decisions.why: Booking the wait as its own category keeps the feature's 'everything measured' purpose. Leaving the wait inside lint's and test build's clocks, with the readers subtracting it, is a mechanism choice whose cost the block states.

decisions.summary: The coverage build lets its slot go before a failed group is asked again a crate at a time
decisions.why: This avoids holding one slot while waiting for a second, part of the no-deadlock mechanism.

decisions.summary: A test's world has no slots (Slots::off()); the slot's own tests name a scratch directory
decisions.why: This isolates the tests from the shared ~/.cache; the mechanism itself is still tested.

blocks: ### T284 (2026-11-26: nothing kept two trees' compiles apart, so the builder count was capped by the chance that they coincide - three builders' anonymous memory peaked at 6.4 GiB of the container's 10 and load at 94 on 22 cores, measured 2026-11-26, `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once")

decisions.summary: Synchronize the checks' compiling cargo calls through a counted set of machine-wide flock slots under ~/.cache/l7r-build-slots/, freed when the holder dies, no daemon; the builder count itself is not capped
decisions.why: This is the GM's request as written (2026-11-26): 'address that with some synchronization rather than pre-emptively limiting builders just in case'. A counted lock on the coinciding compiles is that synchronization, and builders past the count queue only for the compile.

decisions.summary: Every cargo call through cargo_in except cargo fmt, plus cover.rs's coverage build, takes a slot; fmt, llvm-cov show-env/report, cargo --version and direct test-binary runs do not
decisions.why: 'That' in the GM's words is the compiles coinciding. Leaving out the calls that do not compile drops nothing the request reaches, and the measurement puts the peaks in coinciding cover-builds.

decisions.summary: L7R_BUILD_SLOTS defaults to 2 (labeled GUESS) and caps compiling calls at once, not builders; 0 means no slot
decisions.why: A semaphore has to have a count. The default comes from the measured peak (three compiles at once, about 15 rustc each on 22 cores) rather than from a builder cap, and the 0 escape and the knob keep it a tunable piece of synchronization, not a pre-emptive limit on builders.

decisions.summary: If the slot directory cannot be made, a slot file cannot be opened or flock cannot start, the call runs without a slot and says so on stderr
decisions.why: Physically impossible case: when the lock primitive is missing there is nothing to synchronize on. The alternatives are refusing, which is a red gate for a throughput control (nothing in request.md asks for that), or hanging. The stderr notice keeps it visible.

decisions.summary: A wait past L7R_BUILD_SLOT_CEILING (900 s, GUESS) runs the call without a slot, written as a slot-wait line of code 1 with an audit reopen on one such line in a week
decisions.why: Purpose ground: the request is for synchronization that lets more builders work, and an endless wait would let one hung cargo stop every tree's checks for good, which defeats that purpose concretely. The plan states the cost, prices the alternatives and names a falsifier. Aside, non-blocking: 'a pass is then one more compile at once, three' holds for a single pass only. Several starved waiters passing at once under four or five builders are not bounded by it; the slot-wait code-1 lines and the audit's reopen are what would show that.

decisions.summary: Cargo started by a holder carries L7R_BUILD_SLOT_HELD, and a gate run under it takes no slot; a call holds one slot and never waits for a second; the run lock is taken first and the slot inside it
decisions.why: This is deadlock avoidance inside the mechanism. The nested run is already counted under its parent's slot, so no compile goes unsynchronized and the request's reach is not narrowed.

decisions.summary: The wrapper's own tool build (scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh build) takes no slot
decisions.why: The bootstrap argument does not hold, because the slot is a flock program call that shell can make. 'Shell, no Phase line' is implementation cost and is no ground either. The one ground that survives is the measurement: where no check's phase ran, the samples top out at 2.6 GiB and 13 rustc, against 5.9-6.4 GiB where coverage builds coincide (measured 2026-11-26). So leaving this build unslotted does not bring back the coincidence the request is about. The limits are real. The figure is joint with the guard build and comes from one three-builder run, and this is a compile whose coincidence still grows with the builder count. The ruling stands on that measurement and falls with it: the plan's own reopen condition (the re-measurement showing one at a peak) is the right trigger, and the candidate it names should be filed if that happens.

decisions.summary: The hook suites' guard build takes no slot
decisions.why: Ruled on its own, on the same and only surviving ground: the measured ceiling of the no-phase samples (2.6 GiB and 13 rustc, measured 2026-11-26) bounds this build too, well below the coinciding-cover-build peaks. Shell-only is cost, not a ground. This ruling also falls with that measurement, and the three- and four-builder re-measurement is what tests it.

decisions.summary: T284's line's re-measurement of three and four code builders with the slot is not done in this task; the coordinating session runs it once the slot has landed, and docs/process-decisions.md records it as owed
decisions.why: Physical ground: measuring several builders 'with it' needs the slot in every builder's tree, which only a landing gives, so the task cannot do it before it lands. FR-009's filed-task-id rule covers deferred defects, and this is not one. But the payoff of the GM's request (builders no longer pre-emptively limited) arrives only with this re-measurement. Landing T284 alone leaves the builder cap of two in place until it is run and recorded.

decisions.summary: A wait writes one Phase line, step slot-wait, read as its own category ('waiting on a build slot', first of PHASE_COLUMNS) in make task-time and make where-time, with a notice each minute naming the holders; a lint, test build or test run's phase spans its wait and the readers subtract it, while a coverage build's slot is taken before its clock starts
decisions.why: This serves the GM's standing 2026-11-22 words: 'we want everything measured so we know where our time goes, especially for compiling'. A new wait that went unbooked would go against that. Where the clock boundary falls is design, and the readers take the wait out.

decisions.summary: Tests run with Slots::off() and the slot's own tests use a scratch directory; a landing's gate takes the same slot as a builder's
decisions.why: The landing's gate is part of what the cap was protecting ('their compiles and a landing's gate would not coincide'), so covering it keeps the request whole. Tests keeping off ~/.cache is hygiene and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Recorded in dev/audits/build-slot.md (measurement, falsifier, cost, alternatives), docs/process-decisions.md and rust/gate/CLAUDE.md; no make target and no guard added
decisions.why: The audit entry with a falsifier answers the GM's 2026-11-25 register words ('what we would look at that would falsify the notion that this is a good idea'). Adding no target or guard adds nothing the request did not ask for.
